mainTopic: The authority of each generation's leaders, the end of the story of רבן גמליאל and רבי יהושע, and the opening of פרק ראוהו בית דין on how בית דין declares ראש חודש
overview: This amud opens by finishing a ברייתא that teaches that every generation's leaders have full authority. Through פסוקים it shows that ירובעל, בדן, and יפתח count like משה, אהרן, and שמואל in their own time. You must follow the judge of your own days. Next comes the end of the story from the משנה. רבי יהושע came to רבן גמליאל carrying his staff and money. רבן גמליאל greeted him as 'my teacher and my student' and praised a generation where the great listen to the lesser. Then פרק אם אינן מכירין ends, and פרק ראוהו בית דין begins with a משנה about declaring ראש חודש. The גמרא explains each detail of that משנה. A sighting by everyone does not replace בית דין's declaration. The declaration must be made by day, because the פסוק calls it 'משפט'. Judges who saw the moon at night must testify like ordinary witnesses. One judge, even an expert, cannot sanctify the month alone, since even משה needed אהרן. The amud ends by asking whether a witness can become a judge, and it starts quoting a ברייתא from רבי עקיבא that continues on the next amud.

steps.title: שמואל is grouped with משה and אהרן
steps.stepSummary: A second פסוק places שמואל alongside משה and אהרן. Combined with the earlier פסוק that grouped שמואל with ירובעל, בדן, and יפתח, the תורה weighs three minor leaders against three great ones.
steps.simpleTranslation: And it says: 'משה and אהרן among His priests, and שמואל among those who call His name.' The verse weighed three light ones of the world as equal to three weighty ones of the world.
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא brings another פסוק to show that the תורה treats minor leaders as equal to the greatest leaders.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The earlier פסוק listed ירובעל, בדן, and יפתח together with שמואל. This פסוק lists שמואל together with משה and אהרן. Since שמואל appears in both lists, the two groups of three are linked and treated as equal.

keyTerms.meaning: And it says: introduces an additional verse as support
The verse weighed, or treated as equal
The 'light ones' of the world, meaning less distinguished people
The 'weighty ones' of the world, meaning the greatest people

steps.confusionAlert: The 'three light ones' are ירובעל (גדעון), בדן (שמשון), and יפתח from the previous פסוק. The 'three weighty ones' are משה, אהרן, and שמואל. שמואל is the bridge between the two verses.

phrases.english: And it says: 'Moshe and Aharon among His priests
and Shmuel among those who call His name'
phrases.notes: תהלים צט:ו

phrases.english: The verse weighed three light ones of the world
as equal to three weighty ones of the world

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues the ברייתא's earlier proof from the פסוק listing ירובעל, בדן, יפתח, and שמואל.
steps.raayaObject: That minor leaders are treated as equal to the greatest leaders
steps.raayaSupportSource: תהלים צט:ו, read together with שמואל א יב:יא

steps.title: Every appointed leader is like the greatest in his generation
steps.stepSummary: The lesson is drawn: ירובעל is like משה, בדן is like אהרן, and יפתח is like שמואל, each in his own generation. Even the least person, once appointed over the community, has the full status of the greatest.
steps.simpleTranslation: To tell you: ירובעל in his generation is like משה in his generation; בדן in his generation is like אהרן in his generation; יפתח in his generation is like שמואל in his generation. This teaches you that even the lightest of the light, once appointed as a leader over the community, is like the mightiest of the mighty.
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא spells out the lesson of the פסוקים: an appointed leader has full authority, whoever he is.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Each minor leader is matched to one great leader, but only 'in his generation.' The point is not that they were personally as great. The point is that their authority over their own generation was just as binding.

keyTerms.meaning: In his generation
The lightest of the light, the least distinguished person
A leader appointed over the community
The mightiest of the mighty

steps.whatToRemember: Authority comes from the appointment, not from personal greatness. That is why רבי יהושע must accept רבן גמליאל's ruling.
steps.confusionAlert: This does not say ירובעל was personally as holy as משה. It says his rulings carried the same weight for his own generation.
steps.whyThisMatters: This is the core reason רבי יהושע had to submit to רבן גמליאל's בית דין even though he disagreed.

phrases.aramaic: לוֹמַר לָךְ: יְרוּבַּעַל בְּדוֹרוֹ — כְּמֹשֶׁה בְּדוֹרוֹ,
phrases.english: To tell you: Yerubaal in his generation is like Moshe in his generation
Bedan in his generation is like Aharon in his generation
Yiftach in his generation is like Shmuel in his generation
To teach you that even the lightest of the light
who was appointed as leader over the community
is like the mightiest of the mighty

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Draws the explicit lesson from the linkage of verses in step 1.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: Any appointed communal leader has the full authority of the greatest leaders in his own generation.

steps.title: Go to the judge of your own days
steps.stepSummary: The פסוק says to go to 'the judge who will be in those days.' Since nobody could go to a judge from another era, the extra words teach that you must follow the judge of your own time.
steps.simpleTranslation: And it says: 'And you shall come to the priests, the Levites, and to the judge who will be in those days.' Could it enter your mind that a person would go to a judge who was not in his days? Rather, you need only go to the judge of your days.
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא brings another פסוק, asks why it needs the words 'in those days,' and uses them to teach that one must accept the judge of one's own time.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The phrase 'in those days' seems unnecessary, since obviously you can only go to a living judge. Its real lesson is that you may not dismiss your current judge as inferior to earlier ones. The judge of your day is the one with authority.

keyTerms.meaning: Could it enter your mind? (a rhetorical question showing words seem unnecessary)
Judge
In his days, in his own time

phrases.english: And it says: 'And you shall come to the priests, the Levites

phrases.aramaic: וְאֶל הַשֹּׁפֵט אֲשֶׁר יִהְיֶה בַּיָּמִים הָהֵם״,
phrases.english: and to the judge who will be in those days'
phrases.notes: דברים יז:ט

phrases.english: But could it enter your mind
that a person goes to a judge
who was not in his days?
Rather, you have to go only
to the judge who is in your days

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Adds a further פסוק supporting the same principle of each generation's authority.
steps.raayaObject: That one must follow the judge of one's own generation
steps.raayaSupportSource: דברים יז:ט, from the seemingly extra words 'in those days'

steps.title: Do not say earlier days were better
steps.stepSummary: A final פסוק from קהלת warns against claiming that former generations were better than this one.
steps.simpleTranslation: And it says: 'Do not say: How was it that the former days were better than these?'
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא closes its proofs with a פסוק telling a person not to look down on his generation compared to earlier ones.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This fits the theme: a person might think earlier leaders deserved more respect. The פסוק rejects that attitude. One must accept the leaders of his own time.

keyTerms.meaning: The former days, earlier generations
Better than these

steps.whatToRemember: Three proofs (שמואל linked to משה and אהרן, 'the judge in those days,' and 'do not say the former days were better') all teach the same thing: respect and obey your generation's leaders.

phrases.english: And it says: 'Do not say: How was it
that the former days were better than these?'
phrases.notes: קהלת ז:י

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Final supporting פסוק in the same chain of proofs.
steps.raayaObject: That one must not belittle the leaders of one's own generation

steps.title: Quoting the משנה: he took his staff and money
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא returns to the משנה's words: רבי יהושע took his staff and his money in his hand and went to רבן גמליאל.
steps.simpleTranslation: He took his staff and his money in his hand.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא is quoting a line from the משנה to set up the next ברייתא, which adds details about what happened when he arrived.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In the משנה, רבן גמליאל ordered רבי יהושע to come carrying his staff and money on the day that was יום כיפור by רבי יהושע's calculation. Carrying these items breaks the day he thought was holy, which shows his full submission. The quote opens a new section.

keyTerms.meaning: His staff
His money

phrases.english: He took his staff and his money in his hand

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves from the ברייתא of proofs back to the משנה's narrative.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: רבי יהושע obeyed רבן גמליאל and came with his staff and money on his own calculated יום כיפור.

steps.title: רבן גמליאל rises and kisses רבי יהושע
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא relates that when רבן גמליאל saw רבי יהושע, he stood up, kissed him on the head, and greeted him as 'my teacher and my student.'
steps.simpleTranslation: The Rabbis taught: When he saw him, he stood up from his chair and kissed him on his head, and said to him: Peace be upon you, my teacher and my student!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a ברייתא describing how warmly רבן גמליאל received רבי יהושע. The unusual title 'my teacher and my student' is explained in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Even though רבן גמליאל had just forced רבי יהושע to give in, he showed him great honor. The dual title sets up the explanation that follows.

keyTerms.meaning: The Rabbis taught: introduces a ברייתא
He stood up from his chair
My teacher and my student

phrases.english: The Rabbis taught: When he saw him
he stood up from his chair and kissed him on his head

phrases.aramaic: אָמַר לוֹ: שָׁלוֹם עָלֶיךָ רַבִּי וְתַלְמִידִי!
phrases.english: He said to him: Peace be upon you, my teacher and my student!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Expands the משנה's story with a ברייתא.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: רבן גמליאל honored רבי יהושע as both his teacher and his student.

steps.title: Why teacher, and why student
steps.stepSummary: רבן גמליאל explains: 'my teacher' because רבי יהושע taught him תורה publicly, and 'my student' because he obeyed רבן גמליאל's decree like a student.
steps.simpleTranslation: My teacher, because you taught me תורה in public; and my student, because I issue a decree upon you and you fulfill it like a student.
steps.whatsHappening: רבן גמליאל explains the two parts of his greeting.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In wisdom, רבי יהושע was greater and taught רבן גמליאל. In authority, רבן גמליאל was the נשיא, and רבי יהושע obeyed him. Both relationships are true at once.

keyTerms.meaning: In public
Issues a decree
Fulfills it

phrases.english: My teacher, because you taught me Torah in public
and my student, because I issue a decree upon you
and you fulfill it like a student

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Explains the dual title used in step 6.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: רבי יהושע is greater in תורה, but he submits to רבן גמליאל's authority.

steps.title: Fortunate is the generation where the great listen to the lesser
steps.stepSummary: רבן גמליאל praises a generation where greater people obey lesser ones. All the more so, the lesser obey the greater.
steps.simpleTranslation: Fortunate is the generation in which the great listen to the lesser; all the more so the lesser listen to the great.
steps.whatsHappening: The story ends with רבן גמליאל's praise of a generation where people respect authority.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי יהושע (the greater scholar) obeyed רבן גמליאל (the lesser scholar who held authority). A generation where even great people obey is surely one where ordinary people obey too. This ties back to the ברייתא's theme that appointed leaders must be obeyed.

keyTerms.meaning: Fortunate is the generation
Listen to, obey
All the more so (a fortiori)

steps.whatToRemember: The whole section teaches respect for the authority of the leaders of one's generation. Even a greater scholar like רבי יהושע yielded to the נשיא, and he was praised for it.

phrases.english: Fortunate is the generation in which the great listen to the lesser
all the more so the lesser to the great

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Draws the moral from רבי יהושע's submission described in step 7.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: A generation that respects authority, where even the great obey, is praiseworthy.

steps.title: Is it really a קל וחומר?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא objects to רבן גמליאל calling it a קל וחומר that the lesser obey the greater, since that is a plain obligation.
steps.simpleTranslation: A קל וחומר?! It is an obligation!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges the last line of step 8. רבן גמליאל said the small obey the great "all the more so," but the small obeying the great is simply required.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A קל וחומר is used to prove something we would not otherwise know. Everyone already knows the lesser must listen to the greater, so no proof is needed. The wording seems wrong.

keyTerms.meaning: An a fortiori argument: if it is true in the weaker case, it is surely true in the stronger case.
It is an obligation, a plain requirement.

phrases.english: An a fortiori?!
phrases.notes: Said with surprise, questioning the end of רבן גמליאל's statement.

phrases.english: It is an obligation!
phrases.notes: The small must obey the great anyway. No logical proof is needed.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Attacks the wording of רבן גמליאל's conclusion in step 8.
steps.kashyaTarget: רבן גמליאל's phrase that the lesser obey the greater as a קל וחומר.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: A קל וחומר proves a new idea. But the lesser obeying the greater is already an obligation, so calling it a קל וחומר makes no sense.

steps.title: The small reason the קל וחומר for themselves
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא re-reads רבן גמליאל: when the great obey the small, the small conclude on their own that they must surely obey the great.
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather: since the great listen to the small, the small make a קל וחומר for themselves.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers its own question by explaining what רבן גמליאל really meant.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The קל וחומר is not a legal proof of the obligation. It describes how people feel. Seeing a great person like רבי יהושע submit makes ordinary people say, "If he obeys, surely I must," so they obey willingly.

keyTerms.meaning: Since / because of the fact that.
They obey, they listen to.
They apply a קל וחומר to themselves, drawing the lesson on their own.

steps.whatToRemember: רבן גמליאל's praise is about example. When leaders humble themselves, the people learn on their own to respect their leaders.

phrases.english: Rather: since the great ones
phrases.notes: אלא signals a corrected reading of רבן גמליאל's words.

phrases.english: obey the small ones,
phrases.notes: Like רבי יהושע obeying רבן גמליאל.

phrases.english: the small ones apply an a fortiori to themselves.
phrases.notes: They reason: if the great obey, surely we must obey the great.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Resolves the קשיא of step 9 by re-reading רבן גמליאל's words.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: We thought רבן גמליאל was using a קל וחומר to prove the obligation itself.
steps.terutzMaskana: The קל וחומר is the reasoning the small people make on their own, which leads them to obey eagerly.

steps.title: Hadran — Closing פרק אם אינן מכירין
steps.stepSummary: The second פרק of ראש השנה, אם אינן מכירין, ends.
steps.simpleTranslation: We will return to you, "If they do not recognize."
steps.whatsHappening: This is the traditional closing line said at the end of a פרק. It is not an argument. It just marks that the chapter is over.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The name of the פרק comes from its first words, "אם אינן מכירין" (if the court does not recognize the witnesses). Saying הדרן expresses our wish to come back and learn it again.

keyTerms.meaning: We will return to you, the formula for finishing a פרק.
Chapter, named after its opening words.

phrases.english: We will return to you,
phrases.notes: Closing formula.

phrases.english: "If they do not recognize"
phrases.notes: Name of the second פרק of ראש השנה.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Closes the פרק after the story of רבן גמליאל and רבי יהושע.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: The second פרק of מסכת ראש השנה is complete.

steps.title: Not declared before dark: the month becomes 30 days
steps.stepSummary: New פרק ראוהו בית דין: if everyone saw the moon and the witnesses were checked, but בית דין did not say מקודש before nightfall, the month is מעובר.
steps.simpleTranslation: If בית דין and all of ישראל saw the new moon, and the witnesses were questioned, but there was no time to say "Sanctified" before it got dark, the month is made full (30 days).
steps.whatsHappening: A new פרק opens with a משנה. The first case: even though everyone saw the moon, if בית דין did not officially declare it on the 30th day, that day is not ראש חודש.
steps.deeperAnalysis: ראש חודש depends on בית דין's declaration, not just on the moon being seen. Once the 30th day ends without a declaration, the old month gets a 30th day, and ראש חודש moves to the next day.

keyTerms.meaning: The witnesses were questioned and checked by בית דין.
"Sanctified!", the official words declaring ראש חודש.
It got dark, nightfall.
Made full: the previous month gets 30 days.

steps.confusionAlert: Here מעובר does NOT mean a leap year. It means the past month has 30 days instead of 29.
steps.whyThisMatters: This sets a basic rule for the whole פרק. The moon alone does not make ראש חודש. בית דין's declaration does.

phrases.english: If the court and all of Israel saw it [the new moon],
phrases.notes: The opening words רָאוּהוּ בֵּית דִּין also give the new פרק its name.

phrases.english: the witnesses were questioned,
phrases.notes: The testimony was fully checked.

phrases.english: but they did not manage to say "Sanctified"
phrases.notes: The official declaration was missing.

phrases.english: before it got dark,
phrases.notes: The 30th day ended.

phrases.english: it [the month] is made full.
phrases.notes: The previous month becomes 30 days, and ראש חודש is the next day.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Begins a new פרק after the הדרן.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Without בית דין's declaration on the 30th day, the month becomes 30 days, even if everyone saw the moon.

steps.title: Only בית דין saw it: two judges testify
steps.stepSummary: If only the judges saw the moon, two of them testify before the rest, who then declare מקודש מקודש.
steps.simpleTranslation: If only בית דין saw it, two should stand and testify before the others, and they say "Sanctified, sanctified."
steps.whatsHappening: The second case of the משנה: the judges themselves were the ones who saw the moon.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The judges' own sighting does not count by itself here. Two judges become witnesses and testify, and the remaining judges declare the month. The גמרא later asks why this is needed (Step 24), and רבי זירא explains that it is because they saw the moon at night (Step 25).

keyTerms.meaning: Only, alone.
They will testify before them.

phrases.english: If only the court saw it,
phrases.notes: No outside witnesses came.

phrases.english: two should stand and testify before them,
phrases.notes: Two judges act as witnesses before the others.

phrases.english: and they say: "Sanctified, sanctified."
phrases.notes: The court makes the official declaration.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Second case of the same משנה.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: When only the judges saw the moon, two of them testify before the others, who then declare the month.

steps.title: Three judges saw it: form a new court of three
steps.stepSummary: If three judges saw the moon, two testify and seat colleagues next to the remaining one to form a court of three, because a יחיד cannot declare alone.
steps.simpleTranslation: If three saw it and they are a בית דין, two stand up and seat some of their colleagues next to the one left. They testify before them, and the court says "Sanctified, sanctified," because one person alone is not authorized.
steps.whatsHappening: The third case: the court that saw the moon has only three judges. If two become witnesses, only one judge is left.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A court for declaring the month needs three judges. One judge alone cannot do it. So the two witnesses bring in two other colleagues to sit with the remaining judge, making a new court of three that hears the testimony.

keyTerms.meaning: A single individual, here one judge.
Trusted, authorized.
They seat some of their colleagues.

steps.whatToRemember: The month is declared only by בית דין through testimony and a court of three. Seeing the moon, even by everyone or by the judges themselves, is not enough.

phrases.english: If three saw it and they are a court,
phrases.notes: The whole court is just these three.

phrases.english: the two should stand
phrases.notes: Two become witnesses.

phrases.english: and seat some of their colleagues next to the individual,
phrases.notes: This forms a new court of three.

phrases.english: and testify before them,
and they say: "Sanctified, sanctified,"
phrases.notes: The new court declares.

phrases.aramaic: שֶׁאֵין הַיָּחִיד נֶאֱמָן עַל יְדֵי עַצְמוֹ.
phrases.english: because the individual is not authorized by himself.
phrases.notes: The reason a full court of three is needed.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Third case of the משנה. It builds on step 13 for a court with only three judges.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A single judge cannot declare the month. A court of three must hear the testimony and declare it.

steps.title: Why mention that everyone saw the moon?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא opens its discussion of the new משנה by asking why the משנה needs to say that בית דין and all of ישראל saw the moon.
steps.simpleTranslation: גמרא: Why do I need the משנה to teach the case where בית דין and all of ישראל saw the moon?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא begins explaining the new משנה. It asks why the משנה chose the case where literally everyone saw the moon.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The rule is that without a declaration of מקודש before night, the month becomes מעובר. That rule seems obvious for an ordinary case, so why pick such an extreme case? The גמרא assumes the משנה's wording is precise and wants to know what this detail adds.

keyTerms.meaning: The Talmud's discussion of the משנה
Why do I need this? (asks what a detail adds)
To teach / to state in the משנה

phrases.english: Gemara:
phrases.notes: Marks the start of the גמרא on the new משנה

phrases.english: Why do I need it to teach
'the court and all of Israel saw it'?
phrases.notes: Quoting the משנה

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Opens the גמרא on the משנה quoted in step 12
steps.sheelahInformationSought: What does the detail 'everyone saw it' add to the rule?

steps.title: Even a public sighting needs a declaration
steps.stepSummary: The detail is needed. Without it, we might think a sighting this public makes the month new on its own, with no declaration.
steps.simpleTranslation: It was necessary. You might have thought: since בית דין and all of ישראל saw it, the new month is already publicly known, so they should not make the old month מעובר. The משנה teaches us that it is still מעובר.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers that the extreme case teaches something new. Even when everyone saw the moon, there is no new month without the formal declaration.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The הוה אמינא was that public knowledge could replace the formal declaration. The משנה rejects this: only the declaration by בית דין of מקודש creates ראש חודש. A widespread sighting does not.

keyTerms.meaning: It was necessary
It would have entered your mind to say (the mistaken assumption)
It became publicly known
It teaches us (this is what is new)

steps.whyThisMatters: This shows that קידוש החודש depends on the formal act of בית דין, not on the moon simply being seen.

phrases.english: It was necessary, for it would have entered your mind to say:

steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The extreme case teaches that even a fully public sighting does not replace the declaration of מקודש.

steps.title: Why mention witnesses if everyone saw it?
steps.stepSummary: If בית דין itself saw the moon, why does the משנה also mention that witnesses were questioned?
steps.simpleTranslation: But since the משנה already taught that בית דין and all of ישראל saw it, why do I need 'the witnesses were questioned'?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא points out a problem inside the משנה. If the judges saw the moon themselves, why would anyone need to question witnesses?
steps.deeperAnalysis: Witnesses are needed only when בית דין did not see the moon. So the two details seem to contradict each other, or at least make the second one useless.

keyTerms.meaning: But since it taught
The witnesses were questioned

phrases.english: But since it taught

why do I need 'the witnesses were questioned'!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves on to the next detail of the משנה
steps.kashyaTarget: The phrase נחקרו העדים in the משנה
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: If בית דין saw the moon, there is no need for witnesses, so the phrase seems pointless.

steps.title: The witnesses are a second, separate case
steps.stepSummary: The משנה is listing two different cases: either everyone saw it, or witnesses were questioned. In both, if there was no declaration before night, the month is מעובר.
steps.simpleTranslation: This is what the משנה means: alternatively, if the witnesses were questioned but there was no time to say 'מקודש' before nightfall, the month is מעובר.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא re-reads the משנה. The witness detail is not part of the same case but an 'or' case, a second scenario.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The words אי נמי turn the משנה into two cases. In case one, בית דין saw the moon. In case two, witnesses testified and were questioned. Either way, without a declaration before dark, there is no ראש חודש that day.

keyTerms.meaning: This is what it means
Alternatively / or

steps.confusionAlert: Don't read the משנה as one story where everyone saw the moon AND witnesses also came. The גמרא splits it into two separate cases.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the קשיא of step 17
steps.terutzResolutionType: Re-reading the text as two alternative cases
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The משנה describes one case with both a sighting by everyone and questioned witnesses.
steps.terutzMaskana: The משנה describes two separate cases with the same ruling.

steps.title: Why is the witness case needed at all?
steps.stepSummary: If the first case already teaches that nightfall makes the month מעובר, why add a second case about witnesses?
steps.simpleTranslation: But since it already taught that 'before nightfall, it is מעובר,' why do I need it to teach about questioning witnesses at all?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא pushes further. Now that there are two cases with the same ruling, the second case seems to add nothing.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If even a sighting by all of ישראל is not enough without a declaration, then surely witness testimony is not enough either. So the witness case looks repetitive.

keyTerms.meaning: The questioning of the witnesses

phrases.english: But since it taught 'before nightfall, it is made full' —
why do I need it to teach

steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The ruling is already known from the first case, so the second case is repetitive.

steps.title: Questioning witnesses does not let them finish at night
steps.stepSummary: We might have thought that questioning witnesses during the day starts the 'judgment,' so the declaration could be completed at night, as in דיני ממונות. The משנה teaches that it cannot.
steps.simpleTranslation: It was necessary. You might have thought: let the questioning of witnesses be like the start of a court case, and 'מקודש מקודש' be like the end of the case, so they could declare it at night. This would be just like money cases, as the משנה says: in דיני ממונות, they judge in the day and finish at night. So here too they could declare at night. The משנה teaches us that they cannot.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא explains what the witness case adds. Once the court process has begun by day, we might think it can be finished at night. The משנה says no.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The witness case has something the first case lacks: an actual court process (questioning) that began during the day. In דיני ממונות, a case begun by day may end at night. The משנה teaches that קידוש החודש does not follow that rule, so the declaration itself must happen by day.

keyTerms.meaning: The beginning of the court case
The final ruling / end of the case
Money cases
Just like (a comparison)
At night

steps.whatToRemember: Every detail in the משנה teaches something. A public sighting does not replace the declaration. And unlike דיני ממונות, questioning witnesses by day does not allow the declaration of מקודש to be made at night.
steps.whyThisMatters: This sets up the next question in the גמרא: why is קידוש החודש different from דיני ממונות? It will be answered from the פסוק 'כי חק לישראל הוא משפט לאלקי יעקב.'

phrases.english: It was necessary, for it would have entered your mind to say:

so let them sanctify it at night,
just as it is with money cases,
as we learned in a משנה: money cases —

here too they would sanctify at night,
so it teaches us otherwise.

steps.triggerLanguage: אִיצְטְרִיךְ, סָלְקָא דַּעְתָּךְ אָמֵינָא: תֶּיהְוֵי חֲקִירַת עֵדִים כִּתְחִילַּת דִּין

steps.terutzMaskana: Even after the witnesses were questioned by day, the declaration of מקודש cannot be made at night.

steps.title: Maybe the month really is like monetary cases
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks: why not say the declaration of the month really can be finished at night, just like דיני ממונות?
steps.simpleTranslation: But say it really is so!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא pushes back on the answer from Step 20. It asks why the declaration of the month should not really work like monetary cases, where a trial begun by day can be finished at night.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Step 20 said the משנה needed to teach that questioning witnesses by day does not let the declaration finish at night. Now the גמרא asks for a source: what stops us from comparing קידוש החודש to דיני ממונות? This sets up the proof from a פסוק in the next step.

keyTerms.meaning: But say it really is so (a push to accept the rejected idea)
Monetary cases, where judging may begin by day and end at night

phrases.english: But say it really is so?
phrases.notes: Meaning: maybe the declaration CAN be completed at night, like monetary cases.

steps.kashyaTarget: The claim that קידוש החודש cannot be finished at night, unlike דיני ממונות
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Monetary cases may be finished at night once begun by day. Why not apply the same rule here?

steps.title: The verse calls the final declaration a judgment, so it must be by day
steps.stepSummary: The פסוק calls the month's final decree (חק) a 'משפט'. A judgment happens by day, so the final declaration must also be by day.
steps.simpleTranslation: The verse says: 'For it is a decree (חק) for ישראל, a judgment (משפט) of the God of יעקב.' When does it become a 'decree'? At the final ruling. And the תורה calls it a 'judgment.' Just as judgment is by day, here too it is by day.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers with a פסוק from תהלים. It shows that the very moment the month is finalized counts as 'judgment,' and judgment must happen by day.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The month becomes a fixed 'חק' only at the final declaration (גמר דין). The פסוק calls that same moment 'משפט', judgment. In דיני ממונות, only the start must be by day. Here the final ruling itself is called 'judgment', so the final ruling itself must also be by day.

keyTerms.meaning: A fixed decree, here the month once it is finalized
Judgment, which must take place by day
The final ruling (here, declaring 'מקודש')
The Merciful One, meaning the Torah

steps.whatToRemember: The final declaration of the new month must happen in daytime, because the פסוק calls that very moment 'משפט'. This is stricter than דיני ממונות.

phrases.english: The verse states:
"For it is a decree for Israel,

phrases.english: a judgment of the God of Jacob,"

At the final ruling,
and the Torah calls it "judgment";
just as judgment is by day,
so too here, it is by day.

steps.terutzHavaAmina: The month could be finished at night like דיני ממונות
steps.terutzMaskana: The final declaration itself is 'judgment' and must be by day

steps.title: Quoting the משנה: the court itself saw the moon
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes the next line of the משנה: if the בית דין saw the moon, two members testify before the rest.
steps.simpleTranslation: If the court saw it, two should stand and testify before them.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא moves on to the next line of the משנה. It quotes the line to set up a question about it.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Even though the judges saw the moon with their own eyes, the משנה requires two of them to act as formal witnesses before their colleagues. The next step questions why this is needed.

keyTerms.meaning: The court saw it (the new moon)
They should testify before them

phrases.english: If the court saw it,
two should stand
and testify before them.

steps.mimraCoreRuling: When the court sees the moon, two judges must testify before the others

steps.title: Why testify if the judges already saw it?
steps.stepSummary: Hearing testimony should not count more than seeing for yourself. So why do judges who saw the moon need witnesses?
steps.simpleTranslation: And why? Hearing should not be greater than seeing!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges the משנה. If the judges saw the moon themselves, formal testimony seems pointless.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Testimony only tells the court what someone else saw. Here the court saw the moon directly, which is better than being told. So the requirement to testify looks unnecessary.

keyTerms.meaning: Why?
Hearing should not be greater than seeing

phrases.english: And why?
Hearing should not be
greater than seeing!

steps.kashyaTarget: The requirement that judges who saw the moon must testify
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Direct sight by the court is stronger than hearing testimony, so testimony should be unnecessary

steps.title: רבי זירא: they saw it at night
steps.stepSummary: רבי זירא explains that the court saw the moon at night, when it could not act as a court. So the next day they must testify like ordinary witnesses.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי זירא said: The case is where they saw it at night.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי זירא answers the challenge. The משנה is speaking about judges who saw the moon at night.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A court cannot judge or declare the month at night (as proven in Step 22). So what the judges saw at night was not seen 'as a court'. It is just personal knowledge, like any witness has. By day they must testify formally before their colleagues.

steps.terutzHavaAmina: The judges saw the moon as a court, so testimony is pointless

steps.title: Quoting the משנה: three judges saw the moon
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes the next line: if three who are a court saw it, two testify and colleagues are seated with the remaining one.
steps.simpleTranslation: If three saw it and they are a court, two should stand and seat some of their colleagues next to the single one.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא quotes the next case of the משנה to set up another question.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Here the court is only three people, and all three saw the moon. If two become witnesses, only one judge is left. So other colleagues must be seated with him to make a full court.

steps.title: The same question for the three judges
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks the same question here: why testify, if hearing should not count more than seeing?
steps.simpleTranslation: Why? Here too let us say: hearing should not be greater than seeing!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא repeats the earlier challenge, now aimed at the case of three judges.
steps.deeperAnalysis: These three judges saw the moon themselves. Testimony should add nothing to what they already know. So why seat new judges and have two of them testify?

keyTerms.meaning: Here too let us say

phrases.english: Why?
Here too, let us say:

steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Direct sight by the judges should be enough without testimony

steps.title: Answering 'at night' would make the case a repeat
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא blocks the easy answer. If this case is also about seeing at night, it says nothing new beyond the previous case.
steps.simpleTranslation: And if you say here too the case is where they saw it at night, that is the same as the previous case!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא blocks the obvious answer before anyone gives it. Saying 'they saw it at night' would make this case a pointless repeat of the earlier one.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי זירא's answer works for the first case. But using it again here would leave this case teaching nothing new, and a משנה does not repeat itself for no reason. So the question stands, and its answer comes next.

steps.title: The end clause teaches that one judge alone cannot sanctify the month
steps.stepSummary: The case is needed for its end clause, which teaches that one judge is not trusted on his own. Without it, we might have thought an expert could sanctify the month alone, just as an expert may judge money cases alone.
steps.simpleTranslation: The end clause is what we needed: one person alone is not trusted by himself. You might have thought this: we learned that money cases need three judges, but a recognized expert may judge even alone. So here too, let him sanctify the month alone. The משנה comes to teach us otherwise.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers Step 28's challenge. The new lesson of this case is not about the witnessing. It is in the end clause, which requires colleagues to sit with the one remaining judge.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In money cases, a מומחה לרבים may judge alone. So we might have compared קידוש החודש to money cases and let one expert do it. The משנה blocks that comparison by requiring others to be seated with the single remaining judge.

keyTerms.meaning: The end clause of a משנה
A single individual
You might have thought (the mistaken first idea)
Monetary cases
A publicly recognized expert judge

steps.confusionAlert: The new lesson is NOT about the three judges testifying. It is the second half of the case: the one judge left over cannot sanctify the month by himself.

phrases.english: The end clause was what was needed,

phrases.english: that a single person is not trusted by himself.
For you might have thought:
since we learned that money cases are judged by three,

steps.terutzMaskana: One judge, even an expert, cannot sanctify the month alone.

steps.title: Why not let an expert sanctify alone here too?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא pushes back: maybe the comparison to money cases is right, and an expert may sanctify alone.
steps.simpleTranslation: But why not say the same here too?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges the answer from Step 29. Why reject the comparison to money cases?
steps.deeperAnalysis: Step 29 assumed the comparison to money cases is wrong. Here the גמרא asks for a reason. Why shouldn't the expert rule from money cases also apply to sanctifying the month?

steps.title: Even משה needed אהרן with him
steps.stepSummary: No expert was greater than משה רבינו, yet הקב"ה told him to sanctify the month only together with אהרן.
steps.simpleTranslation: There is no greater recognized expert in ישראל than משה רבינו. Yet הקב"ה told him: not until אהרן is with you. As it is written: "And ה׳ spoke to משה and to אהרן in the land of מצרים, saying: This month shall be for you."
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers Step 30 with a proof from the Torah. Sanctifying the month can never be done by one person alone.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The פסוק speaks to both משה and אהרן, and the word "לכם" (for you) is plural. If even משה could not do it alone, no expert can. Since a court cannot have an even number of judges, a third is added, so three are needed.

אהרן, משה's brother
With you
This month shall be for you (plural)

steps.title: Does this mean a witness can become a judge?

steps.deeperAnalysis: The judge who saw the moon is both an eyewitness and a judge on the same matter. That suggests the rule עד נעשה דיין. The גמרא now checks whether this idea fits with other opinions.

steps.title: The משנה may disagree with רבי עקיבא

steps.deeperAnalysis: If the משנה allows עד נעשה דיין, it seems to go against רבי עקיבא's view. The ברייתא's case is judges who personally saw a murder. Their full ruling comes next.
